name: vote
title: Vote
description: A message the room can push up. One control carrying its own count, so there is no second number anywhere in the row and nothing to keep in step. Three states on two attributes, because two of them are independent: `data-gs-voted` is the reader's own press and `data-gs-top` is the room's, a threshold the host sets, so a message can be either, both or neither. The press that casts a vote is the press that takes it back, which is why the control keeps its shape, its width and its place: a control that turned into a figure once pressed would move the next message under the reader's thumb. It ranks nothing and counts nothing. The count is a prop, the threshold is the host's, and a count that ticks by one on a press is the host re-rendering rather than this component guessing.
docs: Put one at the end of a message row. `count` is the host's number and the component never changes it, so an optimistic tick on a press is the host handing back a larger number; `voted` and `top` are likewise host-declared. `voted` is the reader's own vote and is reversible by the same press, so `onVote` fires for both casting and taking back and the host works out which it was from its own state. `top` is the room's top message at whatever threshold the host chose: one message holds it at a time, which is the host's rule to enforce, because this control is shown one message and knows nothing about the others. The row treatment around a top message, the raised bubble specimen 6e draws, belongs to the host: this component draws itself and never reaches into the message beside it.
